probe.format_note: Single 16:9 film, 1920x1080, 60 fps, 1800 frames, 30.08 s. Audio: AAC stereo 48 kHz, continuous for the whole film (no silence of 0.4 s or more below -45 dB), mean -14.9 dB, peak -0.4 dB; content not analysed for beats, third-party audio never reused. The last 3.5 s (26.5 s to the end) are letterboxed with black bars top and bottom.

rights_note: third-party video (file «3d6afef8-2dea-4347-94f7-f96a0cd3a424.mp4»), given by the owner via Downloads/refrencee on 2026-11-03; origin not stated → plan mode ADAPT, never RECREATE

mode.why: third-party product ad of unknown origin: borrow the motion language and look only, never its shots one by one, its object designs, its UI, its copy, its names or logos (owner note). The reference is a software/agent workflow demo (prompt → analysis → plan → build → result → CTA), so UI fits a tool or workflow film; for a plain voiceover package with no tool to show, L4 falls back to REEL and keeps this motion language.

ignored.why: third-party product and company names and logos (the logo lockup written on the mat, the extruded 3D title with a model name and version number); never reused as text, logos or designs; only the motion (lockup writing onto a surface in the scene, a textured 3D title rising out of the surface) is borrowed

the third-party chat app UI (sidebar, model picker, 'connected' badge, input box, send button, status lines, step cards, render viewport, Yes/No dialog, download card) and all its English copy are a third-party product design; only the treatment (a live UI on a 3D laptop screen, text typing in with blur-to-sharp, cards and objects leaving the screen into 3D space, check badges popping) is borrowed

the subjects (rusty pickup photo, toy monster truck, its parts, chassis, roll cage, wheels, the sketch card, the ramp jump) are the reference's story; our scenes take their subjects from the voice-over and are only drawn in this rendering style
the English CTA line, the partner logo lockup and the small availability disclaimer are third-party copy; the end card layout pattern only is borrowed, our outro follows the brand's logo outro
the audio track is third-party music/sound; L6 builds our own sound

method: ffprobe; ffmpeg contact sheets fps=2, 480 px wide, tiled 4x3 (5 sheets covering 0-30 s, all viewed); scene detect gt(scene,0.3) found 3 hard cuts at 18.00, 23.00 and 26.50 s; dense sheets fps=10 (6x2, 1.2 s each, all viewed) over 10.9-12.1 s (lime wipe, not flagged as a cut), 17.4-18.6 s, 22.4-23.6 s and 25.9-27.1 s. Spans read from the 2 fps sheets, accurate to about ±0.25 s, and to about ±0.1 s inside the dense windows. silencedetect + volumedetect on the audio. Colours read by eye, not sampled.

visual_language: A 30 s product-workflow film told as one tabletop toy world: a warm desk is the stage, the laptop screen is the 'mind', and the result leaves the screen and becomes a physical toy on the desk. Medium: stylised soft 3D render with UI screens composited onto 3D devices and floating glass cards, plus a few 2D overlays (status pill, inspection boxes, speed lines, hand-drawn circle). Only 3 hard cuts (18.0, 23.0, 26.5 s); every other change happens in camera: crane down, whip pans, pull-out of a screen, push into a screen or card, a fly-through between foreground objects, a foreground-object wipe, and one brand-colour chevron wipe as a chapter break. Rhythm: 16 beats in 30 s (about 1.9 s each), steady and busy, with frequent snappy pops (badges, pills, confetti) on top of smooth camera moves. Moves: smooth ease-in-out camera pushes and glides (0.5-1.3 s), fast ease-in whips (0.4-0.5 s), snappy overshoot pop-ins (about 0.2-0.3 s) for badges, pills and parts, staggered card slides (about 0.15 s apart), word-by-word blur-to-sharp typing (about 0.1 s per word), linear scan lines and scan rings (0.4-0.6 s). Typography: UI sans for status text, a heavy bold sans for the task headline, a textured extruded 3D title for the opening, a heavy caps action word in a pill, wide-tracked caps for the CTA. Palette: warm peach/apricot desk and wall, cream grid mat, coral/terracotta objects, charcoal darks, white UI, with lime/chartreuse as the energetic accent (cursor, pills, scan lines, wheels) and magenta only as placeholder silhouettes. Signature moments: the logo written on the mat in the overhead opening; the scan line inside viewfinder marks; the glitter cursor clicking send; objects popping out of the screen with confetti; the knolling flat-lay filling from silhouettes with scored inspection boxes; glass step cards with popping check badges; the step-by-step build synced to a self-drawing sketch; the scan ring building the final model; the letterboxed stunt with the CTA typing in behind it.
look: Real 3D (not flat), stylised and toy-like. Materials: matte soft plastic and clay with fine surface speckle/noise (objects, mugs, pencil cup), rough textured stone/cork faces on the 3D title, satin aluminium laptop with charcoal keys, rubber tyres, frosted translucent glass cards with soft white edges, paper with ink line drawing, a sparkly glitter material on the cursor. Light: soft warm key light from a window at the upper right (visible light shafts on the back wall), large soft shadows and contact shadows, warm bounce, gentle bloom on whites and the lime accents. Depth: very shallow depth of field almost everywhere (macro-like toy scale), strong bokeh on desk props, heavy motion blur on whips and fly-throughs. Background: the desk surface and a warm peach wall, never a void; the screen UI is the only clean flat area. Post: fine film grain/halftone dot texture over the whole frame, a soft vignette, slight chromatic aberration (RGB fringing) toward the edges, and a letterbox for the final payoff.
code_translation: Not code-native (3D render). Per D55 it is built as real 3D in code with three.js: a desk plane and wall with warm MeshStandardMaterial plus a subtle noise roughness/bump map for the clay-plastic speckle; rounded boxes and simple primitives for props and toys; a laptop with its screen as a CanvasTexture (UI drawn on a canvas in the brand Persian font, right-to-left, shaped text, Persian digits per data-viz.md), so pushes into and pull-outs of the screen are real camera moves; floating glass cards as rounded boxes with MeshPhysicalMaterial (transmission, roughness for frost) carrying UI canvas textures; warm directional key light with soft shadows (PCFSoft, large shadow radius), hemisphere fill and a window-shaft gobo on the wall; depth of field with a bokeh pass; motion blur by frame blending or directional blur on whips; draw-on tubes via TubeGeometry with an animated drawRange; bottom-up scan-ring builds via an animated clipping plane plus an emissive torus; ghost parts as transparent materials that animate to opaque; knolling silhouettes as flat emissive materials swapped to textured ones behind a wipe mask; film grain, vignette and chromatic aberration as a final shader pass, kept off the text layer so Persian text stays sharp. Status pills, inspection boxes, hand-drawn circle strokes and speed lines can be HTML/SVG overlays composited over the render. Never flattened into 2D shapes, never with joined Persian letters split.
continuity: One tabletop world: every scene is a place on the same desk or on the laptop screen in it, so the camera travels between them instead of cutting.
Screen as a portal: the camera pushes into a device screen to enter the 'thinking', and pulls back out through the bezel to return to the physical world.
Objects leave the screen: results pop out of the screen into the real 3D space, so the digital step becomes a physical object on the desk.
Cursor as actor: an oversized 3D cursor clicks to trigger each new state.
Thinking typed out: status lines and one bold task headline resolve word by word from blur, so the process is always readable as a sentence.
Whole to parts and back: the subject is exploded into a knolling flat-lay, inspected, then rebuilt step by step.
Silhouette to material: placeholders appear as flat colour silhouettes and fill with real material as a wipe crosses them.
Scored inspection: thin boxes draw around a part with a counting score, red for low and green for high.
Plan as cards: steps appear as glass cards in a row, each sealed by a popping check badge while a step counter climbs.
Build in steps synced to a self-drawing sketch and a typing status pill with a progress bar.
Ghost then solid: a part appears translucent first and solidifies when it is placed.
Scan reveal: a scan line (across) or a scan ring (bottom-up) passes over an object and leaves it resolved or built.

Transitions without cuts: whip pans with motion blur, a blurred foreground object passing the lens, a fly-through between two foreground objects, and one full-frame brand-colour patterned wipe as the chapter break.
Accent colour as the 'action' colour: lime marks every active element (cursor, pill, scan line, chosen card), coral marks completion (check badges).
Letterbox for the payoff: black bars arrive for the final stunt and stay on the end card, which is the last scene defocused and washed out.
risks: Third-party ad of unknown origin with third-party product names, logos and UI: ADAPT only. Never copy the brand names, logo lockup, model name and number, the chat app UI, the step cards' copy, the pickup/monster truck story, its parts, the sketch, the ramp stunt, its English copy, its audio or its shot order one by one.

The reference is 16:9 and our default format is 9:16: the wide desk compositions, the row of four step cards and the letterbox must be recomposed vertically (stack cards, crop the desk tighter, letterbox becomes a narrower frame or is dropped), recorded in L5.

Most on-screen text in the reference is tiny UI copy (1-2% of frame height) on a laptop screen: in our film every text that must be read needs the minimum size from safe-zones.md, so push in until the line is readable or lift it to a flat overlay; tiny UI filler stays unreadable on purpose and carries no meaning.

Text typed word by word with blur-to-sharp cannot be read until it lands: every line must finish and hold for the readability hold time; Persian lines type right to left by word, never by split letters.
Counting scores and step counters must show only figures from the approved package (claims accuracy ranks first); Persian digits per data-viz.md.
Grain, halftone dots and chromatic aberration lower the legibility of small text: keep Persian text on a clean layer above the post pass.

Colour mapping: the warm peach world, coral and lime are the reference's colours; L4 maps them onto brand colour roles (base, surface, accent, completion), never its literal hex; colours were read by eye, not sampled. Its materials and light stay (router conflict order, item 4).
Render cost: three.js with soft shadows, bokeh DOF and motion blur at many beats is heavy; build at 30 fps with a capped shadow map and a single DOF pass if render time is a problem.
Audio is third-party, continuous and loud (peak -0.4 dB); it is ignored, L6 builds the sound.
